news.headline: Treasury rally spills over to Indian bonds, debt supply slows move
news.summary: Indian government bonds saw slight gains, reflecting the upward trend in US Treasuries. Investors are keeping a close eye on the forthcoming weekly debt auction, pivotal for market movements. With retail inflation and fluctuating oil prices in play, the Reserve Bank of India may entertain further rate hikes. Although benchmark Brent crude holds steady, it remains vulnerable to geopolitical shifts, prompting caution among traders as they await auction results.

news.headline: Sebi plans consultation paper to remove FPI constraints absent in other markets
news.summary: SEBI is set to release a consultation paper aimed at simplifying regulations for foreign portfolio investors. The goal is to eliminate certain compliance restrictions to enhance India's appeal to global investors. SEBI also plans to expedite the onboarding process, targeting completion in just five business days. Additionally, KYC review cycles for applicable FPIs will be extended, reducing repetitive compliance activities.

news.headline: Rupee climbs past 93/USD as investors seek shelter in Indian stocks, shorts unwind
news.summary: The Indian rupee has strengthened past the 93-per-dollar mark for the first time since April. This recovery is attributed to over $12 billion of foreign investments in Indian equities in November. Hedge funds have unwound bearish positions on the rupee, contributing to its recent gains. The Reserve Bank of India has taken measures to support the local currency amidst stabilization efforts.

news.headline: Anthropic's debut rally fades as shares crack 7% in US pre-market trade
news.summary: Anthropic shares fell as much as 7.4% in premarket trading on their second day, as a global market selloff and concerns over the AI trade overshadowed the optimism surrounding its record-setting IPO debut. After surging 39% from the IPO price on Thursday, the stock ended 17% higher. A steep valuation and competitive threats added to investor caution.

news.headline: Sharp rupee appreciation may cut IT firms' FY27 earnings by up to 13%: Report
news.summary: According to a new report, the appreciation of the Indian rupee could lead Indian IT companies to experience reduced earnings. The stronger rupee against foreign currencies may significantly impact profitability, especially for firms with substantial European exposure. As traditional cost-saving strategies grow scarce, maintaining margins will be a challenge, compounded by the current economic environment affecting pricing strategies in the industry.

news.headline: SELLAS Life Sciences shares plunge 19%: What triggered the sharp sell-off?
news.summary: SELLAS Life Sciences shares plunged nearly 20% after the biotechnology company priced a $150 million public offering at $13 per share, a discount of around 28% to its previous close. The sell-off followed a sharp rally triggered by positive Phase 3 REGAL trial results for its experimental leukemia vaccine.

news.headline: Indian finance hub eyes dual share model to kickstart public offers: Report
news.summary: Indian regulators are currently assessing a new proposal that would allow companies to introduce dual-class shares for listings in both domestic markets and GIFT City. This initiative seeks to invigorate equity market activity in GIFT City, which has faced challenges regarding limited primary market participation. One class of shares would be traded in rupees, while the other would be dollar-denominated, granting foreign investors easier access alongside reduced tax implications.

news.headline: Who is Roaring Kitty? The man behind GameStop's meme rally
news.summary: Keith Gill, better known as Roaring Kitty, is back on social media after nearly two years. His cryptic Cat Mario post sent GameStop shares higher, reviving memories of the 2021 meme-stock rally and sparking fresh interest among retail investors.

news.headline: Rupee rises past 93 vs USD as portfolio inflows, bear retreat fuel rally
news.summary: The Indian rupee has shown remarkable strength, breaking the 93 per dollar barrier for the first time since April. This positive shift was fueled by impressive foreign portfolio investments, exceeding $12 billion in November alone. Consequently, the rupee has left its Asian peers behind as it thrives against a strong dollar, all while navigating the Federal Reserve's anticipated hawkish stance, showcasing an encouraging signal for the Indian market.

news.headline: Rupee strengthens 17 paise to 93.15 against US dollar in early trade
news.summary: Rupee gained 17 paise to trade at 93.15 against the US dollar in early trade on Friday. The appreciation was supported by strong foreign fund inflows into the domestic equity markets. Despite higher crude prices and negative stock market sentiment, the currency showed resilience. Analysts expect slight positive bias in rupee trading due to declining crude and gold prices.
